That death is a LOAD-TIME abort of the whole top-level form, which is

THE FIX.  Pl::Environment::class_bareword_shape($name) -- `\A\p{Lu}` -- the
third member of the shape family that already holds all_caps_shape and
fh_bareword_shape, with the same Unicode rule and the same argument: on an
ASCII name \p{Lu} IS [A-Z], so every ASCII answer is unchanged BY
CONSTRUCTION.  ONE call site (the general indirect-object pre-pass); the
dedicated `new ClassName` pre-pass has no case test at all and is unaffected.

WHY \p{Lu} AND NOT "any identifier start": perl's heuristic does not consult
case, but PCL's narrowing is what keeps `foo Bar` from being read as a method
call when `Bar` is a constant -- widening to \p{XIDStart} would newly read
`cÃ¤ll Ã¤rg` as `Ã¤rg->cÃ¤ll`.  Probed: the lowercase non-ASCII spelling must stay
a function call, and does.

THE NON-UTF8 CASE IS NOT A RISK: perl itself refuses a high-byte identifier
without `use utf8` ("Illegal declaration of subroutine main::f"), and PCL
refuses the file too (PPI cannot tokenize it) -- so a Latin-1 bareword in this
slot is invalid Perl, principle 9.

BARS.  corpus-diff vs 347a46e3 IDENTICAL over 111 files; emission A/B over
571 files (lib/ + cpan-tests/ .pm and .t + t/uni/*.t + perl-tests/*.t +
